briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax-Relief Momentum Builds in Michigan as DEA Rescheduling and Psychedelic Breakthroughs Accelerate Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real signals of relief — both major gubernatorial candidates are now on record against the 24% wholesale tax, and the industry's court challenge is moving toward discovery — while brands keep expanding and competing for shelf space at statewide award shows. Nationally, the DEA has formally urged a judge to move marijuana to Schedule III as psychedelic drugmakers like Compass Pathways close in on what could be the first FDA-approved psilocybin therapy.

local.text: House of Dank has opened its 12th Michigan location in Ann Arbor, a sign that well-capitalized multi-store operators are still expanding even as the wholesale tax squeezes margins statewide.

Michigan's brand-building season is in full swing: the Zalympix 'Grammys of Cannabis' blind judging competition and the statewide Best in Grass Awards are both driving retail traffic and consumer engagement for cultivators looking to break through a crowded, price-compressed market.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James pledged to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale marijuana tax as part of his campaign platform, arguing it hands illicit operators a competitive edge — giving the industry a potential path to relief regardless of who wins in November.

Momentum for repeal is now bipartisan in Lansing: eight state senators filed Senate Bill 810 to scrap the Comprehensive Road Funding Tax Act, arguing the levy represents unnecessary government growth that's hurting licensed operators.

The industry's constitutional challenge to the wholesale tax got a green light to proceed to discovery after a Court of Claims judge ruled questions of fact remain about whether the tax pushes buyers to the illicit market — while 2025 still notched record unit sales despite falling prices, showing underlying demand remains strong.

national.text: The DEA formally urged the judge overseeing the federal rescheduling case to recommend moving marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, filing its final post-hearing brief and citing accepted medical uses for treating anorexia, pain, and nausea.

DEA released the full 2,533-page transcript of the rescheduling hearing this week, documenting government lawyers' case that 'marijuana can no longer remain in Schedule I' — a milestone that sets up a judge's recommendation in the coming months.

Compass Pathways got the FDA's green light for a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for its synthetic psilocybin treatment COMP360, positioning it as the likely first classic psychedelic to reach market for treatment-resistant depression.

FDA finalized its clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and scheduled a September 14 public hearing on psychedelic therapeutics — analysts say the combination signals a more supportive regulatory environment for Compass, Atai, Cybin and GH Research.

Curaleaf escalated its $272 million hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis, arguing the Canadian medical-cannabis giant has failed to deliver shareholder value — while Aurora fired back citing 17% year-over-year revenue growth and record global medical cannabis EBITDA, underscoring how much international expansion is now driving MSO consolidation.
